To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the detection of list catmophisms is possible by means of I/O guided program synthesis and that (2) the use of problem specific templates is feasible in the context of IP.

(1) it is possible to detect the appropriability of a certain template for a given set of input/output examples by using the universality property of higher-order functions; (2) this technique can be used to introduce a catamorphism on lists in our inductive programming system Igor2; (3) the detection of catamorphisms can be done automatically and in an I/O guided way.

(1) the detection of list catanorphisms is feasible by using the universal properties of higher order functions, (2) this detection method can be used to guide the search for programs with list catamorphism templates, and (3) the detection of higher order functions can be extended to other higher order function classes, e.g., to the applicative functor class.
